Active STAR-RIS Empowered Edge System for
Enhanced Energy Efficiency and Task Management
Pyae Sone Aung, Kitae Kim, Member, IEEE, Yan Kyaw Tun, Senior Member, IEEE,
Eui-Nam Huh, Member, IEEE, Zhu Han, Fellow, IEEE, and Choong Seon Hong, Fellow, IEEE,
Abstract—The proliferation of data-intensive, low-latency ap-
plications has driven the adoption of multi-access edge computing
(MEC) to meet the demand for high-performance computing
at the network edge. However, ensuring reliable communication
under non-line-of-sight (NLoS) conditions remains a significant
challenge. While reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) and
the more recent simultaneously transmitting and reflecting RISs
(STAR-RISs) offer promising solutions, their passive nature and
susceptibility to multiplicative fading limit performance gains.
To address these challenges, we propose a novel active STAR-
RIS-assisted MEC system that enhances signal strength and
adaptability by enabling amplification and joint control over
signal transmission and reflection. Our objective is to minimize
the energy consumption of user devices, considering both local
task computation and uplink task offloading, while maintaining
task queue stability. We formulate a joint energy minimization
problem with system constraints and long-term queue stability
requirements. This problem is decomposed into subproblems: (i)
sequential fractional programming is applied to optimize user
transmit power, (ii) convex optimization is used to determine
partial task offloading ratios, and (iii) a modified Lyapunov
optimization combined with double deep Q-networks (DDQN)
is proposed to iteratively solve the active STAR-RIS parameters
(amplitude and phase shift), amplification control, and task
admission at the user side. Numerical results indicate that our
proposed system outperforms the conventional passive STAR-
RIS-assisted system by 18.64% and the conventional passive RIS-
assisted system by 30.43%, respectively.
Index Terms—DDQN, Lyapunov optimization, MEC, simul-
taneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent
surface (STAR-RIS), task queue.
I. INTRODUCTION
A. Background and Motivations
The surge in the adoption of data-intensive and low-latency
applications, including video streaming services, social media
platforms, and online gaming, has driven the evolution of
multi-access edge computing (MEC) as a promising solution.
MEC is a distributed computing paradigm that brings compu-
tational resources and storage capabilities closer to end-users
and their devices at the edge of the network [1]. In MEC

architecture, computing resources are deployed in proximity
to where data is generated or consumed, typically at the base
station (BS) or access point of a cellular network. This enables
low-latency and high-bandwidth processing of data, as well as
efficient delivery of services. Nevertheless, several obstacles,
such as tall structures, may hinder the achievement of line-
of-sight (LoS) communication between the BS and end-users,
which leads to performance degradation.
To mitigate such propagation issues, reconfigurable intelli-
gent surface (RIS) has emerged as a promising technology,
gaining significant attention from academia and industry. An
RIS constitutes a planar meta-surface comprising inexpen-
sive passive elements, programmable via integrated electronic
circuits to adjust the incoming electromagnetic field toward
a desired direction [2]. Although RIS addresses challenges
related to establishing LoS links, its deployment is constrained
by limitations in coverage range and practicality, necessitating
both transmitter and receiver to be situated on the same side.
To overcome this limitation, research focus has shifted
towards the concept of simultaneously transmitting and re-
flecting (STAR)-RIS. As implied by its name, STAR-RIS has
the capability to reflect the incident signal on the same side
while simultaneously transmitting it on the opposite side [3].
STAR-RIS enables full-space (360°) coverage by transmitting
and reflecting incident signals in opposite directions. This
added flexibility increases the degrees of freedom (DoF) in
signal propagation and enhances network capacity. However,
in practical scenarios, the direct link is not completely blocked
by obstacles, resulting in the multiplicative fading effect.
This effect entails the cumulative path loss along the cascade
from the transmitter to the STAR-RIS to the receiver. Unlike
additive fading, multiplicative fading arises from the product
of the path losses between the transmitter and the STAR-
RIS, and between the STAR-RIS and the receiver. Therefore,
achieving significant capacity gains with passive STAR-RIS
configurations becomes unattainable.
In response to this constraint, a new architecture for STAR-
RIS termed active STAR-RIS, has been introduced. Unlike
its passive counterpart, active STAR-RIS can mitigate the
substantial path loss encountered in both the reflected and
transmitted links through its amplification capabilities [4]. This
amplification enables better signal strength, extended cover-
age, and improved energy efficiency, which directly enhances
the computational offloading capabilities of the MEC system,
especially in scenarios requiring high data rates and low-
latency service.

B. Research Contributions
Despite recent advancements, prior studies often assume
idealized task offloading conditions without adequately ad-
dressing task queue dynamics, task admission, and system
stability. This oversight often results in inefficient resource
utilization, task congestion, and inconsistent latency, especially
under dynamic network conditions.
Moreover, existing works mostly focus on passive RIS-aided
MEC systems, which suffer from severe multiplicative fading
and limited signal amplification capabilities, restricting their
effectiveness in obstructed environments. These challenges
highlight a significant research gap in designing an energy-
efficient MEC framework that integrates the active STAR-RIS
with task queue-aware optimization under realistic conditions.
Taking into account the previously mentioned challenges
and motivations, this paper aims to propose an active STAR-
RIS-empowered uplink multi-access edge computing (MEC)
system, where the goal is to minimize user-side energy con-
sumption during local task computation and offloading, while
maintaining task queue stability under practical constraints.
The main contributions of this paper can be summarized as
follows.
• We formulate a joint optimization problem involving
partial task offloading decisions, amplification and phase
shift control of the active STAR-RIS, user transmit power
allocation, and task admission control. The formulated
problem is non-convex, and we propose a multi-stage so-
lution approach based on convex optimization, sequential
fractional programming, and a Lyapunov-based DDQN
framework to handle long-term queue dynamics.
• To be specific, to address the transmit power control prob-
lem, a sequential fractional programming is proposed.
This approach manages the interference without needing
to eliminate it. To address the partial task offloading
problem, an alternative optimization method is introduced
to transform the problem into a convex standard form.
To address the joint amplitude, phase shift, amplifica-
tion, and task admission problem, a modified Lyapunov
optimization with double deep q-network (DDQN) is
developed.
• Finally, to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed sys-
tem compared to benchmark schemes, performance com-
parison has been comprehensively provided and shown
that our proposed system outperforms the conventional
STAR-RIS-assisted by 18.64% and the conventional RIS-
assisted system by 30.43%, respectively.
The remaining portion of the study is organized as follows:
we provide an overview of the related literature in Section II.
Section III represents the system model and problem formula-
tion. Furthermore, Section IV examines the solution strategy,
while Section V provides the performance evaluations. Finally,
Section VI concludes our paper.
II. RELATED WORKS
A. RIS-Assisted Communications
A comprehensive overview of the literature associated with
RIS-assisted communications is discussed in this sub-section
[2], [5]–[9]. In [2], the authors proposed to maximize the
energy efficiency in the RIS-assisted wireless communication
by jointly optimizing the phase shifts and downlink transmit
power, while complying to the the constraints of maximum
power and minimal quality of service. In [5], the authors
studied the the impact of the number of phase shifts on
achievable data rate in uplink RIS-assisted communication
system. In [6], the authors investigated the energy efficiency
maximization with distributed RISs-assisted downlink wire-
less communication system by joint optimization of RIS on-
off, phase and transmit power. In [7], the authors proposed
the energy-efficient downlink communications networks via
multiple aerial RISs by jointly optimizing the aerial RISs
deployment, reflecting elements on-off states, phase shifts
and power control. In [8], the authors studied the RIS-
assisted device-to-device communication by joint optimization
of transmitted power and discrete phase shift in order to
maximize sum-rate. The authors in [9] investigated the impact
on the approximation of ergodic achievable rate for the active
RIS-assisted communication system with different number of
reflecting elements and discrete quantization bits.
Additionally, several researches have been conducted on
RIS-assisted MEC systems [10]–[16]. In [10], the authors
proposed a multi-server MEC system leveraged by multiple
distributed RISs to maximize the task completion rate by
joint optimization of user association, reflecting coefficients of
RISs, receive beamforming vector and computation resource
allocation. In [11], the authors aimed to maximize the energy
efficiency for the RIS-assisted unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-
enabled MEC system under the non-orthogonal multiple ac-
cess (NOMA) protocol. In [12], the authors developed a secure
computation task offloading technique for RIS-assisted MEC
system which includes optimizing RIS deployment to prevent
leaking information to malicious eavesdropper. Nonetheless,
the works mentioned above only considered passive RIS,
which limits the notable capacity gains due to the double
fading effect from the cascaded transmitter-RIS-receiver links.
To solve this, the authors in [13] explored the impact of
amplification on active RIS and its potential enhancement on
achievable rates compared to passive RIS configurations within
identical power constraints. Furthermore, the authors in [14]
presents the hardware architecture model with both passive
elements and a few randomly distributed active elements to
enable the efficient design of the RIs reflection matrices with
low computation overhead. The authors in [15] proposed the
more accurate and practical signal model for the sub-connected
active RIS and investigated the sum-rate maximization prob-
lem to prove the benefits of active RIS elements Moreover,
in [16], the authors proposed methods to maximize the com-
putational latency of the MEC system through the utilization
of active RIS. However, all of the aforementioned works only
considered conventional RIS-assisted systems, which limit the
flexibility and coverage range for the users positioned behind
the RIS.

C. Active STAR-RIS-Assisted Communications
A comprehensive overview of of the literature associated
with active STAR-RIS-assisted communications is addressed
in this sub-section [21]–[24]. In [21], the authors conducted a
performance analysis for the active STAR-RIS-aided two users
wireless communication system, comparing it to the passive
STAR-RIS. The authors of [22] investigated the spectral
efficiency maximization problem for the active STAR-RIS-
assisted massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO)
system under several protocols. Similarly, in [23], the authors
examined to maximize the spectral efficiency and improve the
quality of service (QoS) of the active STAR-RIS-assisted cell-
free mMIMO system system. However, the aforementioned
works have not been carried out on active STAR-RIS-assisted
MEC system. In such a system, active STAR-RIS can mitigate
the inherent path loss in reflected and transmitted links through
amplification. Consequently, it can solve the multiplicative
fading effect, thereby facilitating notable capacity gains for
the users within MEC systems. Furthermore, in [24], the
authors studied the impact of hybrid STAR-RIS with active
transmissive and passive reflective elements to address severe
signal power degradation due to multi-hop transmission.

IV. SOLUTION APPROACH
First of all, to simplify the solution of the complex problem
P1, we divide it into three sub-problems, each focusing on a
specific aspect. We employ sequential fractional programming
for the transmit power control problem, convex optimization
for the partial task offloading problem, and modified Lyapunov
optmization with DDQN for the joint amplitude, phase shift,
amplification, and task admission problem, iteratively.
Employing DRL across the entire optimization problem is
impractical, primarily because the combined action spaces
for all control variables in problem P1 would be excessively
large, complicating the learning process for the DRL agent.
Therefore, we adopt a three-step approach iteratively to miti-
gate this issue and streamline the DRL process. Considering
previous studies such as [40] and [41], it is feasible to solve
one or more decision variables via an optimization approach
while determining the rest of the variables through a machine
learning approach to minimize computational demands.1 Ini-
tially, we address the transmit power control problem using
a sequential fractional programming method in Section IV-A
and convex optimization for the partial task offloading problem
independently to reduce the action space in Section IV-B.
Subsequently, we tackle the remaining optimization problem
through the Lyapunov optimization with DRL approach in
Section IV-C.

DRL is a suitable solution approach due to its ability to
handle high-dimensional, non-linear, and complex decision

techniques, DRL does not require the problem to be convex

explicit modeling is challenging or infeasible.
Among DRL methods, DDQN is particularly suitable for
several reasons. DDQN effectively addresses the overestima-
tion bias present in standard Q-learning by decoupling action
selection and value estimation, resulting in more stable and
accurate learning [49]. This is crucial for environments with a
large number of possible actions and uncertain outcomes, as
it ensures more reliable value approximations.

state. The agent then receives a reward from the environment.
This stochastic policy, ˆπ(a|s) = Pr(An = a|Sn = s),
represents the likelihood of selecting action a in state s at
time n. The objective of the agent is to develop a policy that
optimizes the expected total reward over time, which can be
expressed mathematically as the sum of cumulative rewards,

VI. CONCLUSION
In this article, we have studied an active STAR-RIS-assisted
MEC system. To minimize the energy consumption of the user
devices during local task computation and uplink transmis-
sion, we formulated a joint partial task offloading, amplitude,
phase shift coefficients, amplification coefficients, user trans-
mit power and task admission at the user devices problem.
We decomposed the problem into three sub-problems due
to its non-convexity, dynamic environment, and task arrivals.
To solve these sub-problems, we implemented sequential
fractional programming, convex optimization, and Lyapunov
optimization with DDQN. Numerical findings indicate that our
proposed system system surpasses the conventional STAR-
RIS-assisted system by 18.64% and the conventional RIS-
assisted system by 30.43%, respectively. This is due to the
effective utilization of amplification and greater DoF of active
STAR-RIS. Moreover, we conducted a comparison with the
DQN and MAB methods to show the improvement due to the
mitigation of the overestimation bias of the DDQN method.
The performance is enhanced by 5.88% and 21.31% compared
to the DQN and MAB methods, respectively.
In addition, we compare with greedy offloading and cen-
tralized queue systems to demonstrate the benefits of incorpo-
rating task queue management and ensuring long-term queue
stability. The Lyapunov approach ensures queue stability by
making decisions that respond to real-time queue states, while
DDQN enables the system to learn optimal policies over
time, even in the absence of a precise environment model.
This synergy allows the system to handle fluctuations in
task arrivals and varying wireless conditions by continuously
updating control actions based on observed system states. As
a result, the proposed framework maintains energy efficiency
and queue stability even under sudden changes, making it
well-suited for practical deployment in highly dynamic MEC
scenarios.
The proposed active STAR-RIS-assisted MEC system has
strong potential for real-world implementation. Active STAR-
RIS can be integrated into existing infrastructure, such as
building facades, with power supplied either through wired
connections or energy-harvesting techniques. The use of
model-free DDQN allows the system to adapt to dynamic
wireless conditions without requiring precise prior knowledge,
making it suitable for complex urban environments with
varying traffic and channel conditions. In terms of scalability,
our approach supports a growing number of users and active
STAR-RIS elements, due to the modular problem decompo-
sition and efficient training of the DRL agent. These charac-
teristics make the proposed framework a practical solution for
large-scale deployment in future networks that require high
energy efficiency and low-latency performance.
It is worth noting that our current formulation assumes
perfect channel state information (CSI) and ideal hardware
conditions. However, in practical deployments, especially for
active STAR-RIS, channel estimation errors and hardware
impairments (such as non-linear amplification, phase noise,
and quantization errors) may degrade system performance.
Future work will aim to extend the proposed model to include
robust learning-based methods that can adapt to such imper-
fections. Incorporating realistic channel estimation techniques
and modeling non-linear amplification behavior will allow for
more accurate performance analysis and control in real-world
deployments.

Abstract: The proliferation of data-intensive, low-latency ap- plications has driven the adoption of multi-access edge computing (MEC) to meet the demand for high-performance computing at the network edge. However, ensuring reliable communication under non-line-of-sight (NLoS) conditions remains a significant challenge. While reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) and the more recent simultaneously transmitting and reflecting RISs (STAR-RISs) offer promising solutions, their passive nature and susceptibility to multiplicative fading limit performance gains. To address these challenges, we propose a novel active STAR- RIS-assisted MEC system that enhances signal strength and adaptability by enabling amplification and joint control over signal transmission and reflection. Our objective is to minimize the energy consumption of user devices, considering both local task computation and uplink task offloading, while maintaining task queue stability. We formulate a joint energy minimization problem with system constraints and long-term queue stability requirements. This problem is decomposed into subproblems: (i) sequential fractional programming is applied to optimize user transmit power, (ii) convex optimization is used to determine partial task offloading ratios, and (iii) a modified Lyapunov optimization combined with double deep Q-networks (DDQN) is proposed to iteratively solve the active STAR-RIS parameters (amplitude and phase shift), amplification control, and task admission at the user side. Numerical results indicate that our proposed system outperforms the conventional passive STAR- RIS-assisted system by 18.64% and the conventional passive RIS- assisted system by 30.43%, respectively.
